ApprovedTarget.description:
The operator-issued scope for one automation target. Existence of a matching,
unexpired, un-released scope is the owner's standing consent for that exact
(kind, target) pair; a worker can never mint one.

ArtifactRead.description:
Authenticated read of a CAS object over the control socket. The object bytes are
base64-encoded in the JSON reply so raw, digest-verified bytes can cross the
1 MiB frame; the CLI decodes and streams them to stdout. Objects beyond the
recoverable IPC budget are refused with `artifact_too_large_for_ipc`, never truncated.

CommandResult.description:
The typed success payload of a `CoreReply::Ok`. One variant per public
`CoreCommand`, tagged by the command's serde `type` via the `command` field,
carrying that command's actual leaf result type. A reply can only ever
unwrap the variant whose command matches the request; a mismatched or echoed
payload fails serde (unknown/missing command tag) and the TS validator
(`packages/contracts/src/validate.ts` + `ResultOf<C>`) before any consumer
sees it. Intentional user JSON stays an explicitly bounded `serde_json::Value`
inside the leaf DTOs (e.g. `canonical_args`), never this envelope.

DomainQualifications.description:
All qualification records for a domain: the live enabled one (if any)
plus the blocked (revoked/failed) ones, newest first.

Empty.description:
The unit result of commands whose leaf outcome carries no value. Serde
renders it `{}`, matching the pre-envelope wire shape of those replies.

EvaluationReportInput.description:
The TS `EvaluationReport`, re-derivable and re-gated here. `state` and
`reasons` on the wire are ignored: the core re-derives them from the raw
counts before persisting anything.

RunReceipt.description:
What `RunCreate` returns: the durable identities a caller needs to drive the
run, plus the state it was born in.

RunResolution.description:
Resolution asserts only the expected run set, never authorizes a state
transition. Terminal run state must already be committed by C4.

oneOf.description: The operator's own adapter: the only caller that may open a scope.

A bounded coding worker: receives broker requests only, never the host
session bus or the operator's personal browser.

ShutdownReceipt.description: `Shutdown {}` reply: the daemon acknowledged the request.

StatusReport.description:
`Status {}` reply: durable counters, all on the exact numeric wire (counts
are SQLite integers, not JS-safe by construction).

TargetKind.description:
A target kind the broker may scope authority over. `DocumentFile` is the
core-owned, byte-verified document model (the offline-qualifiable backend);
`BrowserProfile` and `NativeWindow` are live backends that require the
pinned AlphaCode executor.

WebGptActivationState.description: Activation state of a WebGPT connection as observed by the core.

oneOf.description: The pinned sidecar bundle is not present under the core data dir.
The sidecar is present and pinned, but no owner activation exists yet.
The owner has activated the isolated profile; a genuine turn can run.

Present but unusable: non-bridge connection, pinned sidecar digest
mismatch, or a profile that drifted after activation. Never used
silently.

WebGptStatus.description:
The observed WebGPT connection state. `reason` is the exact, non-secret
cause whenever the state is not `Activated`.

WebGptSubmissionReceipt.description:
A durable WebGPT submission receipt. `idempotency_key` is the frame request
ID (the durable identity); `digest` is the receipt's own SHA-256 (over the
receipt content excluding the digest field) and its CAS path is
`webgpt_submission/<key>/<digest>`.

image_digests.description:
Image parts the sidecar received, as CAS objects owned by the run's
project; each digest is the image bytes' content digest.

native_message_id.description:
The native message id exactly as the sidecar wrote it. Absent when the
send could not be confirmed.

original.description: Set on a duplicate view: the digest of the original send's receipt.

profile_digest.description:
The profile digest at send time, binding the receipt to the exact
activation the turn ran under.

prompt_text.description: The prompt text (all text parts, in order), kept for the audit trail.

reason.description: Human-readable cause for non-submitted states (never a secret).

sidecar_version.description: The pinned sidecar version that produced this receipt.

submission_digest.description:
SHA-256 of the canonical content; a same-key/different-content submit is
a conflict, never a silent overwrite.

superseded_by.description: Set on a superseded view: the digest of the resubmit receipt.

WebGptSubmissionState.description: Terminal state of one WebGPT submission.

oneOf.description: The pinned sidecar confirmed the native send (native_message_id present).

The sidecar failed, or recovery found no native confirmation (unknown
outcome — explicit, never implicitly retried).

A repeat of the same idempotency key and content: the stored receipt is
returned, no second native send happens.

Superseded by a `resubmit`: retained for the audit trail; the original
receipt's identity is unchanged, this view adds `superseded_by`.

WebGptTurnInput.description:
Input to a genuine WebGPT turn (W2). Image parts carry base64 inline data
(`data:<mime>;base64,<data>`); every image is stored in the run's project
CAS before the sidecar runs.

conversation_id.description:
Native conversation to continue, when the sidecar reports one. A turn
never opens a fresh chat implicitly: continuation only follows a
sidecar-confirmed conversation id, never a retry of a failed send.

WebGptTurnOutput.description: The native WebGPT response with its provenance.

conversation_id.description: Native conversation identifier as reported by the sidecar.

model.description:
The native model label as reported by the sidecar; the core never
substitutes its own identity.

native_message_id.description:
The native message id exactly as the sidecar wrote it (its
confirmation file — not core-generated).

response_text.description: The native reply text exactly as the sidecar returned it.
